title: Count Flink Restarts in Splunk With OpenTelemetry: 3 Pod Deletions, 7 Restarts
description: I deleted a Flink TaskManager pod 5 times on EKS. In the first 2, job state blinked for 5 s and Splunk's Kubernetes metrics didn't move. Then 3 deletions made 7 Flink restarts, and the OpenTelemetry Flink receiver put exactly 7 in Splunk.
linkedin:
Your Flink job says RUNNING. Your pods look healthy.
It may still be restarting.

I deleted a TaskManager pod 5 times on EKS:
→ Job state, first 2 deletions: RESTARTING for about 5 s, then RUNNING again
→ Kubernetes metrics in Splunk, first 2 deletions: available 1, container restarts 0

Flink's own counter: 3 deletions, 7 restarts.
With the OpenTelemetry Flink receiver, Splunk counted 7 too, at the same two instants.
Each restart was in a Splunk point 17 to 21 s later.

I ran the upstream contrib Collector next to the Splunk agent for it. The whole config is in the post.

Every step and the raw output:
{LINKS}

Next, I'm proposing a restart-time metric for the OpenTelemetry Flink receiver.

body:
I deleted a Flink TaskManager pod five times on EKS, in two phases. In the first two deletions, Flink restarted the job and reported RUNNING again about 5 seconds later, Kubernetes had a new pod Ready in 2 seconds, and **the Kubernetes metrics in Splunk Observability Cloud didn't move**: available replicas 1 in every 10 s point, container restarts 0.

Flink's own restart counter told a different story. In the second phase, **3 pod deletions added 7 to Flink's `numRestarts`**, and with the **OpenTelemetry Flink receiver** sending to Splunk, Splunk's `flink.job.restart.count` rose by **exactly 7** over the same window. Each restart was in a Splunk data point 17 to 21 seconds after Flink's REST API showed it.

> **TL;DR**
> - Job state: the first RESTARTING stretch after each deletion lasted 5.0 to 5.1 s. A dashboard that polls state every 10 s or more can miss stretches that short.
> - Kubernetes view in Splunk, first two deletions: `k8s.deployment.available` stayed at 1 in every 10 s point (rollup min) while `kubectl` saw 0 for about 2 s, and `k8s.container.restarts` stayed at 0, because a deleted pod is replaced, not restarted.
> - Flink's restart counter: +1 per deletion in the first phase, but +3, +2 and +2 in the second. Splunk's counter matched Flink's REST API: +7 and +7.
> - The receiver also sent checkpoint counters and JVM GC for both the JobManager and the TaskManagers: 29 `flink.*` metric names in all.

![Flink's numRestarts read every second against Splunk's flink.job.restart.count in 10 second points, both rising from 2 to 9 over three pod deletions](/abhimanyu/articles/count-flink-restarts-in-splunk-with-opentelemetry-3-pod/cover.png)

## Why restarts, not job state

A Flink job with a restart strategy heals itself: lose a TaskManager and it goes RESTARTING, then RUNNING again. For background on watching restarts and checkpoints, see Flink's [monitoring guide](https://flink.apache.org/2019/02/21/monitoring-apache-flink-applications-101/) and the [AWS Managed Flink lifecycle post](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/big-data/part-2-deep-dive-into-the-amazon-managed-service-for-apache-fink-application-lifecycle). Two Flink issues frame what I measured: [FLINK-23807](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-23807) ("use numRestarts to detect restarts in tests") and [FLINK-34907](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-34907) ("jobRunningTs should be the timestamp that all tasks are running").

I'm a code owner of the OpenTelemetry Flink metrics receiver, so I wanted numbers: what job state, Kubernetes and Splunk each show when a TaskManager disappears, and whether the receiver's restart count in Splunk matches Flink's own.

## The setup

- **EKS**, two nodes. Flink 1.20.5 (`flink:1.20-java17`) as a session cluster: one JobManager, one TaskManager with 2 slots.
- **The job:** Flink's StateMachine example at parallelism 2, checkpoints every 5 s, fixed-delay restarts with a 5 s delay.
- **Splunk OTel Collector chart 0.163.1** on the cluster, which sends the Kubernetes metrics.
- **A watcher** on the other node read Flink's REST API once a second: job state, tasks running, `numRestarts`, checkpoint counts, plus Flink's own state-change timestamps.
- **Deleting the TaskManager pod** stands in for losing a TaskManager pod, as in a node drain or an eviction. I didn't test out-of-memory kills or containers restarting in place.

Phase 1 had no Flink receiver and two deletions 45 s apart. Phase 2 added the receiver and three deletions 49 to 54 s apart (the lab waits for RUNNING, then 30 s).

## Phase 1: what job state and Kubernetes showed

Two deletions, 45 seconds apart:

| Deletion | Flink RESTARTING after | Not RUNNING | New pod Ready after | `kubectl` available min | Splunk available min | Flink restarts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1.2 s | 5.1 s | 2.0 s | 0 | 1 | +1 |
| 2 | 1.1 s | 5.0 s | 2.0 s | 0 | 1 | +1 |

"Not RUNNING" runs from Flink's RESTARTING timestamp to its next RUNNING timestamp. My one-second samples never caught the job saying RUNNING with a task not yet running, so a RUNNING-before-tasks gap like the one FLINK-34907 is about didn't show at this sampling; a gap under a second could still be there.

`kubectl` read 0 available TaskManagers for about 2 seconds each time. I read `k8s.deployment.available` in Splunk with `rollup='min'`, so a dip inside a 10 s point would survive, and every point was 1. The chart sets no `collection_interval` for its `k8s_cluster` receiver, which reports every 10 s by default, so a 2-second replacement usually falls between two reports. That's why Flink's own restart counter is the signal to bring into Splunk for this.

`k8s.container.restarts` stayed at 0 too. Splunk held a series for 3 TaskManager pods: the original and two replacements, each with 0 restarts. A deleted pod is replaced, so the restart count of a container never moves.

![Splunk chart of k8s.deployment.available for flink-taskmanager with rollup min, from my Splunk org](/abhimanyu/articles/count-flink-restarts-in-splunk-with-opentelemetry-3-pod/step-1.png)

## Phase 2: the receiver in Splunk

For the Flink receiver I ran the upstream contrib Collector (0.165.0) next to the Splunk agent, sending OTLP to the agent on its node. This is the config from the lab's `k8s/30-collector.yaml`:

```yaml
receivers:
  flink_metrics:
    endpoint: http://flink-jobmanager:8081
    collection_interval: 10s
processors:
  resource:
    attributes:
      - {key: deployment.environment, value: flink-lab, action: upsert}
  batch:
    timeout: 5s
exporters:
  otlphttp:
    endpoint: http://${env:HOST_IP}:4318
service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [flink_metrics]
      processors: [resource, batch]
      exporters: [otlphttp]
```

`HOST_IP` comes from the pod's `status.hostIP`. Collector 0.165.0 logs that `otlphttp` is a deprecated alias for `otlp_http`.

Then three more deletions. Flink's `numRestarts` rose by 3 for the first, then 2 and 2: 7 restarts from 3 deletions. The first RESTARTING stretch after each was still 5.0 s, but it wasn't the whole story: the job was back at RUNNING with its count settled 21, 16 and 16 s after the deletions, and the watcher saw RESTARTING in 33 of 152 one-second samples, against 8 of 80 in phase 1.

To compare like with like, the lab read both counts at the same two instants, 11:24:50 and 11:27:20 UTC, with no restart within 15 seconds of either:

| | At 11:24:50 | At 11:27:20 | Increase |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flink REST API `numRestarts` | 2 | 9 | +7 |
| Splunk `flink.job.restart.count` | 2 | 9 | +7 |

Splunk lists `flink.job.restart.count` as a `CUMULATIVE_COUNTER`, and I read it with `rollup='latest'`, so each point holds the running total, not a per-point delta. Here's the chart in Splunk, with the same SignalFlow:

```text
data('flink.job.restart.count', filter=filter('deployment.environment', 'flink-lab'), rollup='latest').max().publish()
```

![Splunk chart of flink.job.restart.count rising in steps from 2 to 9 between 11:25 and 11:27 UTC](/abhimanyu/articles/count-flink-restarts-in-splunk-with-opentelemetry-3-pod/step-2.png)

## How soon Splunk showed each restart

For each of the 7 restarts, from the second Flink's REST API first showed it:

- **To the end of the first 10 s Splunk point holding it:** 17 to 21 s.
- **To a Splunk query that returned it**, polling every 3 s during the deletions: 20 to 25 s.

The receiver reads every 10 s and the batch processor waits up to 5 s, so most of that delay is the path I chose. A 5 s `collection_interval` should shorten it; I didn't test that.

## Checkpoints and JVM GC

Between the same two instants, failed checkpoints matched: +2 in Flink, +2 in Splunk. Completed checkpoints were +53 in Flink's REST API and +58 in Splunk. A 10 s Splunk point holds a value scraped somewhere inside it, and with a checkpoint every 5 s that timing can shift each instant by about 2, so up to about 4 overall. A gap of 5 is more than timing explains, and I didn't find the rest. Until then, I'd use completed checkpoints in Splunk as a rate, not an exact tally.

`flink.jvm.gc.collections.count` arrived for the JobManager (G1 young and old generation, 2 series) and for the TaskManagers (8 series across the pods).

## Run it in your own account in 3 steps

### Step 1: Create the cluster (the EKS cluster took 7m28s in my run)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Abhimanyu9988/showmerit.git
cd showmerit/labs/count-flink-restarts-in-splunk-with-opentelemetry-3-pod
export AWS_REGION=eu-central-1 TF_VAR_region=eu-central-1 LAB_NAME=flink-lab TF_VAR_lab_name=flink-lab
export SPLUNK_REALM=us1 SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=your-ingest-token SPLUNK_API_TOKEN=your-api-token
terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve
```

### Step 2: Without the receiver (about 6 minutes)

Run `./reproduce.sh`. It installs the Splunk OTel Collector chart, starts Flink and the job, deletes the TaskManager twice, and reads the Kubernetes metrics back from Splunk next to `kubectl`.

### Step 3: With the receiver (about 4 minutes)

Run `./fix.sh`. It starts the contrib Collector with the Flink receiver, deletes the TaskManager three more times, and compares Splunk's counters with Flink's REST API at the same instants.

To alert on it, a detector on the increase of `flink.job.restart.count` per job over a few minutes catches restarts that job state and pod health don't show.

## Help build it

Flink can report how long a job has spent in each state in total. Its [metrics page](https://nightlies.apache.org/flink/flink-docs-release-1.20/docs/ops/metrics/) lists `<jobStatus>TimeTotal`, in milliseconds (so `restartingTimeTotal` for RESTARTING), and says whether these metrics are reported depends on the `metrics.job.status.enable` setting, for example:

```yaml
metrics.job.status.enable: [CURRENT_TIME, TOTAL_TIME]
```

In this run, the only `flink.job.*` metrics the receiver sent were the checkpoint count, checkpoints in progress, the last checkpoint's size and time, and the restart count: no time spent restarting. A total like that would keep a 5-second outage even with a 10-second scrape. I'm opening an issue to add it as an optional metric; if you'd like to build it, I'm happy to help you get started.

## Clean up (the cluster costs money while it runs)

```bash
./cleanup.sh
terraform destroy -auto-approve
```

## What I didn't test

- **Why some deletions counted more than one restart.** The first phase counted one per deletion and the second phase two or three, with the receiver running and the deletions 49 to 54 s apart instead of 45 s. I recorded the counts, not the cause.
- **Total time not RUNNING per deletion** when it counted several restarts. I measured the first RESTARTING stretch and the RESTARTING samples per phase.
- **Other failures:** a crashing job, a lost JobManager, or a node failure. Only TaskManager pod deletions.
- **Scale.** One job, one TaskManager with 2 slots, one restart strategy, and a 10 s collection interval.
